_note: The little solar system that turns on the home page. Every number lives here.

view._note: The drawing's own coordinate box. CSS scales it; nothing here is in screen pixels.

time._note: Earth takes earthLapSeconds to go round. Every other body is timed from its REAL orbit in days, so the order is honest: Mercury-ward is fast, Jupiter is slow. compression squashes the range, because a true-to-scale Jupiter (11.9 Earth years) would sit still on a home page. At 0.55 the ordering is kept and the slowest lap is about 4x the fastest instead of 12x.

orbit._note: The dashed rings. Spacing is by the square root of the distance, so Earth is not swallowed by the Sun while Jupiter still stays in the picture.

probe._note: A spacecraft of our own, out between Mars and Jupiter on the long way round.
probe.label: a spacecraft on its way

startAngles._note: Where everything sits at the moment the page opens, in degrees. Chosen so nothing overlaps on the first frame.
